n: Received on April 6, 1830, the day the Church was organized. The Lord commands that a record be kept, in which Joseph will be called seer, translator, prophet, apostle, and elder — titles describing his roles.

f.w: there shall be a record kept among you

f.g: one who sees by divine power things hidden or yet to come.

n: The Holy Ghost inspired Joseph to lay the Church’s foundation and build it up in “the most holy faith.”
The date of the Church’s organization is recorded: April 6, 1830.

f.w: the sixth day of the month which is called April

n: The Church must give heed to all the words and commandments the prophet receives, living in holiness.

f.w: give heed unto all his words

n: Members are to receive the prophet’s word as if from the Lord’s own mouth, with patience and faith. Patience is needed because not every instruction is immediately understood.

f.w: as if from mine own mouth

n: Following the prophet brings protection: the gates of hell won’t prevail, darkness will be dispersed, and heaven will shake for their good.

f.w: the gates of hell shall not prevail against you
cause the heavens to shake for your good

n: The Lord has inspired Joseph to advance Zion with great power, and he knows Joseph’s diligence and prayers.
The Lord has seen Joseph weep for Zion; now his time of rejoicing has come, with forgiveness of sins and blessings on his work.
Those laboring in God’s vineyard will be greatly blessed and will believe the prophet’s words, which testify through the Holy Ghost that Jesus was crucified for the world’s sins.

f.w: the remission of sins unto the contrite heart

n: Joseph is to be ordained by Oliver Cowdery, called here an apostle.
In turn, Oliver is to be an elder under Joseph’s hand. On this day they ordained each other elders after the members voted to accept them as teachers.

f.w: this church of Christ, bearing my name

n: Oliver is to be the Church’s first preacher, to members and the world, to Gentiles and also — emphatically — to the Jews.

f.w: the first preacher of this church
f.g: Oliver gave the first public discourse of the Church on April 11, 1830.
